To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the isolated, perfusion rat liver from alloxan diabetic, fasted rats is a useful model for studying the effect of insulin in vivo on hepatic metabolism.

the isolated, perfuse alloxan-diabetes rat liver is capable of maintaining elevated rates of gluconeogenisis, ureogenisis, and amino acid and ketone body release when compared to normal, fasted rat livers.
insulin has an anti-catabolic action on the perfused, alloxan-diabetes rat liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of insulin in vitro upon the metabolism of the perfused liver of the alloxan-diabete rat.
the effect of insulin on the metabolism of the isolated, perfuse rat liver.
the regulation of gluconeogenesis in the isolated, perfusion rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin is an important regulator of the rate of hepatic glucose output and that insulin is a regulator of hepatic gluconeogenesis.

in the perfused alloxant diabetic rat liver, insulin has an immediate effect in suppressing the catabolic process of gluconeogenesis as well as ureogenesis and ketogenesis, and in stimulating glycogen deposition.
in the fasted state the alloxan diabetic rat liver is in a hypercatabolic condition and insulin reverses this state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver of the alloxan diabetic rat is in a state of hypercatabolism and that the addition of insulin in vitro to the perfusion fluid of such livers suppresses the hypercatabolic state.
insulin is the major factor in determining whether the diabetic liver will catabolize or synthesize glucose.
the insulin effect on gluconeogenesis and amino acid release in the perfused alloxant diabetic rat liver is mediated by an inhibition of the rate of gluconeogenic substrate entry into the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin is an anti-catabolic hormone, which can be used to suppress the elevated rates of gluconeogenic, ureogenic, ketogenic and amino acid release observed with alloxan-diabetes.
insulin has immediate anti-cataboic effects in perfused diabetic liver.

insulin has a rapid effect in the diabetic liver, which is not due solely to a change in perfusate lactate concentration, and that the anti-catabolic action of insulin in the diabetic liver may involve more than one mechanism.
